title: pressure-snapshot-consolidated-datapull-2026-06-28
content:
Purpose:
This sheet consolidates raw telemetry and event pulls used for the capacity postmortem of the 2026-06-25 regional saturation incident. The goal is to produce a compact, queryable snapshot (timeseries + event joins) to answer: where did pressure originate, how did queueing evolve, which hosts/regions hit throttles, and what spillover/eviction patterns we observed.

Summary / quick findings (high level):
- Incident window: 2026-06-25T13:10:00Z -> 2026-06-25T15:45:00Z (primary spike at ~13:40Z).
- Root observation: sudden workload surge from EU-west region ingest pipeline caused sustained host-level GPU utilization > 94% for ~22 minutes; autoscaler reacted but new pods came up after 8-10min, causing queue growth and edge-level throttles in two AZs (eu-west-1a and eu-west-1c).
- Spillover: requests routed to fallback capacity in eu-central for 14% of incoming traffic during the peak; that routing increased cross-region P99 by ~120ms.
- Notable: KV-cache evictions on model-x-2b due to rapid context size increase; this reduced effective throughput and increased tokenization CPU pressure.

Datasets pulled (BigQuery table names / prometheus metrics):
- bigquery:infra_gpu.telemetry.hourly (historical hourly aggregates)
- bigquery:infra_gpu.telemetry.raw_events (per-request telemetry w/ request_id, host, model, tokens_in/tokens_out)
- bigquery:infra_gpu.queue_events_v2 (enqueue/dequeue timestamps, host, queue_depth)
- bigquery:infra_gpu.throttle_logs (throttle_reason, target_route, region, request_id)
- prometheus: gpu_utilization_ratio{region,host} (1m resolution)
- prometheus: queue_length_per_host{region,host,model} (1m)
- cloud provider logs: gke.preemptions and node_pool_scale_events

Primary SQL & PromQL extracts used (copyable):
1) Host-level max utilization window (BigQuery SQL):
SELECT host, region, MAX(utilization) AS max_util,
  COUNTIF(utilization > 0.9) AS minutes_over_90pct,
  ANY_VALUE(node_pool) AS node_pool
FROM `infra_gpu.telemetry.raw_events`
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-06-25T12:50:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-06-25T16:00:00Z')
GROUP BY host, region
ORDER BY max_util DESC
LIMIT 200;

2) Queue growth timeline (PromQL, 1m step):
sum by (region) (queue_length_per_host)
  [2026-06-25T12:50:00Z:2026-06-25T16:00:00Z]
(note: exported as CSV via Grafana snapshot)

3) Throttle event join (BigQuery):
SELECT t.timestamp, t.request_id, t.throttle_reason, q.host, q.model, q.enqueue_time, q.dequeue_time, TIMESTAMP_DIFF(q.dequeue_time, q.enqueue_time, SECOND) AS queue_secs
FROM `infra_gpu.throttle_logs` t
LEFT JOIN `infra_gpu.queue_events_v2` q ON t.request_id = q.request_id
WHERE t.timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-06-25T13:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-06-25T14:30:00Z')
ORDER BY t.timestamp ASC
LIMIT 5000;

4) KV-cache eviction correlate (BigQuery):
SELECT model, host, COUNTIF(event_type = 'kv_eviction') AS evictions, AVG(context_len) AS avg_ctx_len
FROM `infra_gpu.telemetry.raw_events`
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-06-25T13:20:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-06-25T14:10:00Z')
GROUP BY model, host
HAVING evictions > 0
ORDER BY evictions DESC;

Field notes on pull decisions: 
- We pulled raw_events at request granularity only for the incident window + 30m pre/post to reduce export size. Full-day raw pull was too big (>120GB).
- Aggregates (hourly) were included for baseline comparison (prior 7 days same hour weekday patterns).
- Prometheus 1m resolution used for utilization and queue_length; 15s would be prettier but retention/exports were limited.

Sample extracted CSV rows (representative, redacted):
timestamp,region,host,model,utilization,queue_secs,throttle_reason
2026-06-25T13:38:47Z,eu-west-1,host-12,model-x-2b,0.958,12,none
2026-06-25T13:39:11Z,eu-west-1,host-12,model-x-2b,0.961,34,queue_timeout
2026-06-25T13:40:05Z,eu-west-1,host-15,model-x-2b,0.973,52,throttle_global_qps
2026-06-25T13:42:20Z,eu-west-1c,host-21,model-rerank-1,0.88,5,none

Observations from joined tables: 
- Hosts with >20 minutes_over_90pct correlate with queues >30s and >3 throttle events in 10min window.
- Two node pools (np-eu-highmem-3, np-eu-gpu-batch) showed slower autoscaler scale-up due to the NodePool max-pod-per-node setting and horizontal autoscaler cooldown policy.
- Cross-region fallback was triggered earlier than expected; fallback policy thresholds were too sensitive to transient queue spikes.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate: 
- Did upstream client(s) change request fanout pattern around 13:35Z? (See linked GA event IDs in slack thread.)
- Was there concurrent heavy retraining maintenance in eu-west that increased shared storage IO causing secondary CPU pressure on inference nodes? Need storage IO metrics.
- Are there host labels we can add to better identify 'burst-friendly' pools at routing time?

Immediate action items (post-pull):
- [Owner: Liam Chen] Short-term: increase reserved capacity in eu-west by +3 GPU nodes for weekdays 13:00-16:00 for one week. (ETA: 2026-07-03)
- [Owner: Priya Kapoor] Medium-term: relax fallback sensitivity and add 30s debounce before cross-region fallback triggers. (ETA: 2026-07-14)
- [Owner: Theo Martinez] Investigation: correlate storage IO (GCE agent) with CPU steal and container restarts for the incident hosts. Pull histograms for 2026-06-25. (ETA: 2026-07-05)
- [Owner: Sana Patel] Data follow-up: export full queue_events_v2 for affected hosts for the entire week around the incident and run model-level queue length decomposition. (ETA: 2026-07-02)

Notes / scratch: 
- Slack snippets: at ~13:37Z ops saw first throttle, alert suppressed due to alert grouping -> consider alert grouping policy tweak.
- Local dev note: re-run the throttle join with LIMIT removed when analysts confirm export location. Current export: gs://redwood-ops-exports/infra/2026-06-25/pressure-snapshot.csv
- TODO: attach Grafana snapshots (utilization and queue timeline) to Confluence postmortem page.

Attachment manifest (exports produced):
- gs://redwood-ops-exports/infra/2026-06-25/pressure-snapshot.csv (primary join, ~1.2M rows, 2.4GB gzipped)
- gs://redwood-ops-exports/infra/2026-06-25/prometheus_gpu_util_eu-west_1m.csv.gz (1m series for incident window)
- gs://redwood-ops-exports/infra/2026-06-25/throttle_events_sample.csv (5000 rows sampled)

Authors notes (informal):
- This pull felt heavier than past incidents because of KV-cache evictions cascading into queue growth; need to add a synthetic test that exercises long contexts at scale during canary windows.
- We trimmed some fields (user_agent, full_prompt) to avoid PII in exported artifacts; saved raw with redaction map locally.

If you need additional slices (by model family, by customer tier, or full-request traces), say which and I'll re-run targeted joins.

End of sheet.
